cards.front: Recall a key point about Operational Amplifiers
cards.back: An operational amplifier (op-amp) is a high-gain differential amplifier with two inputs: inverting (−) and non-inverting (+).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Operational Amplifiers
cards.back: The ideal op-amp has infinite open-loop gain, infinite input impedance, zero output impedance and infinite bandwidth.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Operational Amplifiers
cards.back: A real op-amp has very high but finite open-loop gain (typically 10⁵ to 10⁶), high input impedance and low output impedance.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Operational Amplifiers
cards.back: Negative feedback is used to control gain and improve stability; it reduces overall gain to a predictable value set by external components.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Operational Amplifiers
cards.back: The inverting amplifier configuration has the input signal applied to the inverting input via Rin with feedback resistor Rf from output to inverting input.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Operational Amplifiers
cards.back: Gain of an inverting amplifier: Av = −Rf/Rin; the output is 180° out of phase with the input.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Operational Amplifiers
cards.back: The non-inverting amplifier has the input applied to the non-inverting input; feedback via a voltage divider to the inverting input.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Operational Amplifiers
cards.back: Gain of a non-inverting amplifier: Av = 1 + Rf/R1; the output is in phase with the input.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Operational Amplifiers
cards.back: The virtual earth (virtual ground) principle: when negative feedback is applied, the two inputs are at virtually the same potential.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Operational Amplifiers
cards.back: Op-amps require dual-rail power supplies (typically ±15 V) or single-rail with a virtual mid-rail reference.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Operational Amplifiers
cards.back: Slew rate limits how fast the output voltage can change, measured in V/µs.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Operational Amplifiers
cards.back: Input bias currents are small currents that flow into the op-amp inputs; they can cause offset errors in precision circuits.
